WALCL.name: Fed assets
WALCL.note: Fed's total balance-sheet assets. Rising = more liquidity into the system.

WRESBAL.name: Bank reserves at Fed
WRESBAL.note: Cash banks hold at the Fed. Falling reserves often mean tighter money-market conditions.

RRPONTSYD.name: Overnight reverse repo
RRPONTSYD.note: Overnight reverse repo — cash parked at the Fed. Rise drains money available to markets.

WTREGEN.name: Treasury cash account
WTREGEN.note: Treasury General Account — the government's Fed checking account. Rise pulls reserves out of banks.

WSHOSHO.name: Fed securities held
WSHOSHO.note: Securities the Fed holds outright (QE stock). Core of balance-sheet liquidity.

M2SL.name: US money supply (M2)
M2SL.note: Broad US money supply (cash, checking, savings). Slow growth can signal tight credit.

TOTLL.name: US bank loans & leases
TOTLL.note: Total bank loans & leases. Credit still flowing to the real economy.

BUSLOANS.name: Business bank loans
BUSLOANS.note: Bank lending to businesses. Soft = firms borrowing less or banks tightening.

GFDEBTN.name: US federal debt
GFDEBTN.note: Total US federal debt outstanding. Stock of government paper, not the monthly deficit.

TRESEGCNM052N.name: China FX reserves
TRESEGCNM052N.note: China's foreign-exchange reserves. Proxy for Asia USD liquidity and China capital flows.

ECBASSETS.name: ECB assets
ECBASSETS.note: European Central Bank balance sheet. Euro-area QE/QT pulse.

JPNASSETS.name: Bank of Japan assets
JPNASSETS.note: Bank of Japan assets. Japan still a huge global liquidity source.

SOFR.name: SOFR overnight rate
SOFR.note: Secured Overnight Financing Rate — US overnight secured funding cost. Higher = tighter cash.

EFFR.name: Fed funds rate
EFFR.note: Effective Federal Funds Rate — where overnight bank reserves actually trade vs the Fed target.

DGS3MO.name: US 3-month yield
DGS3MO.note: 3-month Treasury yield. Short-rate anchor near Fed policy.

DGS2.name: US 2-year yield
DGS2.note: 2-year Treasury yield. Highly sensitive to near-term Fed path.

DGS5.name: US 5-year yield
DGS5.note: 5-year Treasury yield. Mid-curve — mix of policy path and growth/inflation views.

DGS10.name: US 10-year yield
DGS10.note: 10-year Treasury yield. Benchmark long rate for mortgages, corporates, and risk assets.

DGS30.name: US 30-year yield
DGS30.note: 30-year Treasury yield. Ultra-long duration; sensitive to term premium and fiscal supply.

T10Y2Y.name: 2s10s curve
T10Y2Y.note: 10y minus 2y curve. Negative (inverted) often warns of slowdown; steepening can ease long-end conditions.

T10Y3M.name: 3m10s curve
T10Y3M.note: 10y minus 3m curve. Another recession-signal spread; deeper inversion = tighter credit impulse.

DFII5.name: 5-year real yield
DFII5.note: 5-year TIPS real yield. Cost of real (inflation-adjusted) money for the medium term.

DFII10.name: 10-year real yield
DFII10.note: 10-year TIPS real yield. Higher real yields = tighter financial conditions for risk assets.

T5YIE.name: 5-year inflation bet
T5YIE.note: 5-year breakeven inflation — market's expected average CPI over 5 years.

T10YIE.name: 10-year inflation bet
T10YIE.note: 10-year breakeven inflation — market's long-run inflation pricing.

T5YIFR.name: 5y5y forward inflation
T5YIFR.note: 5y5y forward inflation — inflation expected 5–10 years out. Fed's preferred long-run gauge.

DTWEXBGS.name: Broad US dollar index
DTWEXBGS.note: Fed broad dollar trade-weighted index. Stronger dollar = tighter USD liquidity abroad.

RBUSBIS.name: Real dollar index
RBUSBIS.note: BIS real effective USD — inflation-adjusted dollar strength vs trading partners.

IRLTLT01DEM156N.name: German 10-year yield
IRLTLT01DEM156N.note: German 10-year Bund yield. Euro risk-free long rate.

IRLTLT01GBM156N.name: UK 10-year yield
IRLTLT01GBM156N.note: UK 10-year Gilt yield. UK risk-free long rate.

IRLTLT01JPM156N.name: Japan 10-year yield
IRLTLT01JPM156N.note: Japan 10-year JGB yield. Global duration and BoJ policy pulse.

MOVE.name: Bond volatility (MOVE)
MOVE.note: ICE BofA MOVE — implied vol on Treasuries. Bond-market fear gauge (VIX for rates).

DXY.name: Dollar index (DXY)
DXY.note: ICE US Dollar Index vs majors (EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF). Classic DXY tape.

EURUSD.name: Euro vs dollar
EURUSD.note: Euros per dollar. Higher = stronger euro / weaker dollar.

USDJPY.name: Dollar vs yen
USDJPY.note: Yen per dollar. Higher = stronger dollar vs yen (often risk-off or rate-gap driven).

USDCNH.name: Dollar vs yuan
USDCNH.note: Offshore yuan per dollar. Higher = weaker CNH; China/EM stress tell.

GBPUSD.name: Pound vs dollar
GBPUSD.note: Pounds per dollar. Higher = stronger sterling.

AUDUSD.name: Aussie vs dollar
AUDUSD.note: Aussie dollar vs USD. Risk/commodity-linked FX.

USDMXN.name: Dollar vs peso
USDMXN.note: Pesos per dollar. Higher = weaker peso; EM stress proxy.

STICKY_CPI.name: Sticky CPI
STICKY_CPI.note: Atlanta Fed sticky CPI — prices that change rarely. Persistence of inflation.

INDPRO.name: Industrial production
INDPRO.note: US industrial production index. Factory and utility output pulse.

PAYEMS.name: Nonfarm payrolls
PAYEMS.note: Nonfarm payrolls — monthly jobs added. Headline labor-market print.

UNRATE.name: Unemployment rate
UNRATE.note: Unemployment rate. Rising = labor market cooling (soft for growth).

ICSA.name: Initial jobless claims
ICSA.note: Initial jobless claims — weekly new unemployment filings. Fast labor stress tell.

CCSA.name: Continuing claims
CCSA.note: Continuing claims — people still on unemployment. Stickier labor softening.

JTSJOL.name: Job openings
JTSJOL.note: JOLTS job openings. Labor demand; falling openings = cooling.

JTSQUR.name: Quit rate
JTSQUR.note: JOLTS quit rate. Workers' confidence quitting — high = tight labor market.

CES0500000003.name: Average hourly earnings
CES0500000003.note: Average hourly earnings. Wage pressure into inflation and margins.

RSAFS.name: Retail sales
RSAFS.note: Advance retail sales. Consumer spending pulse (nominal).

DGORDER.name: Durable goods orders
DGORDER.note: Durable goods orders. Capex and goods-demand lead.

HOUST.name: Housing starts
HOUST.note: Housing starts. New residential construction — rate-sensitive growth.

PERMIT.name: Building permits
PERMIT.note: Building permits. Forward look at housing starts.

CPIAUCSL.name: Headline CPI
CPIAUCSL.note: Headline CPI (all items). What households feel; noisy month to month.

CPILFESL.name: Core CPI
CPILFESL.note: Core CPI (ex food & energy). Fed's preferred CPI underlying read.

PCEPI.name: Headline PCE
PCEPI.note: Headline PCE price index — Fed's official inflation target basket.

PCEPILFE.name: Core PCE
PCEPILFE.note: Core PCE (ex food & energy). The Fed's main inflation target series.

MICH.name: Inflation expectations
MICH.note: UMich 1-year inflation expectations. Household inflation psychology.

GDPC1.name: Real GDP
GDPC1.note: Real GDP (chained). Quarterly growth of the whole economy.

COPPER.name: Copper
COPPER.note: Copper futures. "Dr. Copper" — industrial demand / global growth proxy.

VIX.name: Equity volatility (VIX)
VIX.note: Cboe VIX — 30-day implied vol on the S&P 500. Equity fear gauge.

BAMLH0A0HYM2.name: High-yield spread
BAMLH0A0HYM2.note: ICE BofA high-yield OAS. Extra yield junk bonds demand over Treasuries. Credit stress.

BAMLC0A0CM.name: IG credit spread
BAMLC0A0CM.note: ICE BofA investment-grade OAS. Extra yield on IG corporates — milder credit stress.

NFCI.name: Financial conditions
NFCI.note: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index. Higher = tighter US financial conditions.

ANFCI.name: Adjusted financial cond.
ANFCI.note: Adjusted NFCI — strips out economic activity so it's more about pure financial stress.

SPX.name: S&P 500
SPX.note: S&P 500. Broad US large-cap equity risk appetite.

NDX.name: Nasdaq 100
NDX.note: Nasdaq-100. US mega-cap / growth equity tape.

RTY.name: Russell 2000
RTY.note: Russell 2000. US small-cap risk — more domestic and credit-sensitive.

GOLD.name: Gold
GOLD.note: Gold futures. Real-rate / dollar / fear hedge — treat as an output, not a cause.

BTC.name: Bitcoin
BTC.note: Bitcoin. Speculative liquidity-sensitive risk asset — output, not input.

WTI.name: WTI crude oil
WTI.note: West Texas Intermediate crude. US oil benchmark.

MTSDS133FMS.name: Fed budget balance
MTSDS133FMS.note: Monthly federal budget balance. Deficit (−) means more Treasury issuance ahead.

ROW_UST.name: Foreign Treasury holdings
ROW_UST.note: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries. Soft = overseas buyers stepping back.

TREAST.name: Fed Treasury holdings
TREAST.note: Fed's SOMA Treasury holdings — the QE/QT Treasury piece of the balance sheet.

FYGFDPUN.name: Debt held by public
FYGFDPUN.note: Debt held by the public (ex Fed/gov accounts). The stock markets actually finance.

DFEDTARU.name: Fed funds target (top)
DFEDTARU.note: Top of the Fed's federal funds target range. Official policy rate ceiling.

DFEDTARL.name: Fed funds target (low)
DFEDTARL.note: Bottom of the Fed's federal funds target range. Official policy rate floor.

MORTGAGE30US.name: 30-year mortgage rate
MORTGAGE30US.note: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Direct hit to housing and consumer duration.

THREEFFTP10.name: 10y term premium
THREEFFTP10.note: NY Fed ACM 10y forward term premium — extra yield for long-bond risk, beyond rate-path expectations.

THREEFFTP2.name: 2y term premium
THREEFFTP2.note: NY Fed ACM 2y forward term premium — near-term bond risk premium.

T10YFF.name: 10y vs fed funds
T10YFF.note: 10y yield minus fed funds. Positive steepness vs policy; compressed = tighter/longer-end caution.

USDCHF.name: Dollar vs franc
USDCHF.note: Swiss francs per dollar. Higher = stronger USD / weaker CHF safe-haven bid fading.

USDCAD.name: Dollar vs loonie
USDCAD.note: Canadian dollars per dollar. Oil- and NAFTA-sensitive cross.

USDBRL.name: Dollar vs real
USDBRL.note: Reais per dollar. Higher = weaker BRL; EM stress proxy.

EURJPY.name: Euro vs yen
EURJPY.note: Euro vs yen. Classic risk-on cross — rises when risk appetite improves.

EMPIRE_MFG.name: Empire manufacturing
EMPIRE_MFG.note: NY Fed Empire State manufacturing survey. Regional PMI-style activity.

PHILLY_MFG.name: Philly manufacturing
PHILLY_MFG.note: Philly Fed manufacturing survey. Another regional PMI-style read.

CFNAI.name: Chicago Fed activity
CFNAI.note: Chicago Fed National Activity Index. Broad monthly growth factor (0 ≈ trend).

WEI.name: Weekly economic index
WEI.note: NY Fed Weekly Economic Index. High-frequency real activity blend.

CSUSHPISA.name: Case-Shiller home prices
CSUSHPISA.note: Case-Shiller home price index. National house-price level.

EXHOSLUSM495S.name: Existing home sales
EXHOSLUSM495S.note: Existing home sales. Housing turnover — rates and affordability.

UMCSENT.name: Consumer sentiment
UMCSENT.note: University of Michigan consumer sentiment. Soft demand / mood gauge.

PPIACO.name: Commodity PPI
PPIACO.note: PPI all commodities. Upstream goods inflation.

PPIFIS.name: Final-demand PPI
PPIFIS.note: PPI final demand. Pipeline prices into consumer inflation.

MEDIAN_CPI.name: Median CPI
MEDIAN_CPI.note: Cleveland Fed median CPI. Robust underlying inflation (less noisy than mean).

TRIMMED_CPI.name: Trimmed-mean CPI
TRIMMED_CPI.note: Cleveland Fed trimmed-mean CPI. Another core-like inflation measure.

SHELTER_CPI.name: CPI shelter
SHELTER_CPI.note: CPI shelter. Housing rents/OER — big, sticky CPI weight.

SUPERCORE.name: Services CPI ex energy
SUPERCORE.note: CPI services ex energy. "Supercore" — services inflation the Fed watches.

CORESTICK.name: Sticky core CPI
CORESTICK.note: Atlanta Fed sticky core CPI. Core prices that are slow to change.

BBB_OAS.name: BBB credit spread
BBB_OAS.note: BBB corporate OAS. Credit spread for the weakest IG bucket — early stress tell.

HY_CCC_OAS.name: CCC credit spread
HY_CCC_OAS.note: CCC high-yield OAS. Distressed credit; blows out in risk-off.

EPU.name: Policy uncertainty
EPU.note: Economic Policy Uncertainty index. News-based US policy risk.

SAHM.name: Sahm recession rule
SAHM.note: Sahm rule trigger — unemployment jump vs recent low. Recession flag when ≥0.5.

HYG.name: High-yield bond ETF
HYG.note: iShares High Yield Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for HY credit (up = easier).

LQD.name: IG bond ETF
LQD.note: iShares IG Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for investment-grade credit.

SKEW.name: Crash-insurance skew
SKEW.note: Cboe SKEW — price of S&P crash insurance (tail risk). Higher = more fear of a crash.

SILVER.name: Silver
SILVER.note: Silver futures. Precious metal with industrial demand too.

TLT.name: Long Treasury ETF
TLT.note: iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF. Long-bond price tape (up = yields down).

EWZ.name: Brazil equity ETF
EWZ.note: iShares MSCI Brazil ETF. EM equity risk proxy.

NET_LIQ.name: Net liquidity
NET_LIQ.note: Street shorthand: Fed assets − TGA − ON RRP. Rising = more cash in markets.

STOCK_BOND_CORR.name: Stock–bond correlation
STOCK_BOND_CORR.note: 60-day correlation of stocks vs bonds (sign-flipped). Rising together = less diversification.

formula.lights: Per light: median of member scores (each = mean of sign×2y z and flipped 5y %ile). Clubs are small complementary sets; Street table keeps the rest. Score >+0.45 / <−0.45 paints the word. Inflation upside = hot.
